name: Multi-head Latent Attention · MLA + QK-norm
tagline: Compress keys and values into a 256-dimensional latent, then normalize q and k.
description: Queries pass through a rank-768 latent. One joint down-projection gives a rank-256 key/value latent and a single RoPE key shared by all heads; per-head content keys and values are reconstructed from the latent, as in DeepSeek-V2. The native shell's per-head QK RMSNorm with gain 1.2 then acts on every reconstructed query and key after RoPE, bounding each logit by 1.44·√128 ≈ 16.3, the same bound as in MHA, MQA and GQA.
paperTitle: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
mechanism: Query latent rank 768; joint key/value latent rank 256 plus one shared RoPE key
12 heads: QK content 64 + RoPE 64, value 128, reconstructed explicitly
Per-head QK RMSNorm × 1.2 after RoPE; full causal attention in 26 layers
limitations: The QK normalization departs from DeepSeek-V2, which has none, and stops the key up-projection from being absorbed into the query; value absorption and the latent are unchanged. Latent-cache decoding is not implemented, so no KV-cache saving is claimed. Value embeddings are disabled, and the matching multi-head control without them has not been trained. Single seed 42; trained from the frozen Others branch, not yet ported to the current code.
